open_obligations: Check that the authors' own results show gains over the solo-verifier baseline (p9 L48-L55) of a kind comparable to Khan et al.'s judge-accuracy gains
Note that the authors do not test whether stronger provers help more, which is the capability part of Khan et al.'s claim
out.other_title: Debate helps non-expert LLM and human judges on QuALITY; persuasive debaters help more
out.rationale: The authors explicitly place their results alongside Khan et al.'s debate results as part of a growing body of work which tentatively suggests that scalable oversight techniques may be increasingly viable, which is SUPPORTS. Settings differ: Khan et al. use debate on the QuALITY comprehension task, where the expert debaters have information that the non-expert judges lack, while the from-record's setting names trained prover-verifier protocols on code validation and graph isomorphism. Khan et al.'s non-expert judges include humans as well as models, and the non-expert models are otherwise as capable as the experts, whereas the from-record's setting pairs GPT-4o provers with GPT-4o-mini verifiers and names no human judges, so the agreement does not extend to human judges.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether interaction with stronger models helps a weaker judge or verifier; the agreement is tentative and holds at the level of overall direction, not specific accuracy numbers
